purpose: Interactive Fiction Weaver compile of a Low Sere lower-step household's custodian-support turn, testing whether care for Sera Venn can remain real without hiding food, witness, and family costs.
tonal_mode: Warm domestic wit under institutional fatigue, tightening into quiet material pressure.
artifact_role: Playable illustrated-fiction website collateral and Kalsa lore stress test; not canonical simulation state and not core social-model training signal.

local_awareness_summary.text: Bel Orra is a lower-step water witness who knows her household's wet wall, missed labor, ration marks, safe public areas of the Cistern House, and the terms of the forty-second-bowl turn. She does not know the Ashen Intake's hidden configuration.

Sera Venn holds provisional authority for ordinary inspection, isolation, degraded service, and material refusal at the Cistern House boundary; a meal or household witness does not appoint her or enlarge that authority.
Maro Seln controls the settlement drain wheel and records the basin table's water and work obligations. He does not control Sera's pressure spindle or technical stop.
Nim Orra is fixture-local elaboration of Bel's already-mentioned eldest: a young adult carrying household water and missing Grey Bed labor while the lower-step wall worsens.

frame_controls.text: Playable perspective remains Bel's ordinary human viewpoint from her lower-step hearth to the public Cistern House threshold. Choices use food, household reports, safe cleaning work, witness presence, withdrawal, and neighborhood exchange rather than technical machine control.
The opening establishes supper, damp bedding, carried water, missed bed work, and the household joke before the pressure seal interrupts routine.

authority_boundaries.text: Bel may report household conditions, perform instructed outer-screen cleaning, witness observable work, withhold her household's voluntary support, and organize exchanges. She may not operate the pressure seal, declare the intake safe, or appoint a custodian.

Sera alone among the scene participants owns the named technical isolation and degraded-service decisions; she must narrow service when safe support is absent rather than treat lonely work as success.
Maro may turn the drain wheel, call household replacements, and record obligations, but cannot convert a meal token or witness mark into technical competence.

object_custody.text: Bel's hearth controls its food, dampness strip, work chit, and clay turn-token until delivery. The communal bowl carries support evidence but owns no authority. Sera controls the sampling vessel, isolation catch, and safe outer-screen work instruction. Maro controls the drain wheel and basin ledger.

required_semantics.text: Food delivered, custodian recovery, household observation, witness coverage, missed work, service scope, and private household safety remain separate state surfaces after branches fold.
Every ending must make loyalty, accurate record, household boundary, or neighborhood reciprocity preserve something and cost something else; no value becomes the universal correct answer.
The forty-second bowl may support a person and expose a site-support failure, but cannot certify Sera, settle Teren's appeal, or decide post-descent custody.

forbidden_resolutions.text: Do not advance the canonical three-shutter pressure clock, resolve the Ashen Intake descent, recover the Ashen Measure, or decide Sera's appointment.
Do not turn the Low Sere bowl into a Kalsa-wide kinship custom, universal currency, legal court, technical rite, or separate institution.
Do not make Bel know hidden dungeon evidence or machine causality; she can preserve observed knocks, marks, water, ash, and instructions without explaining their ultimate cause.

branch_and_fold_plan.summary: Four choice layers fold household portion, custodian delivery, a bounded witness interval, and the final obligation record into eight state-gated endings.

branches.actor_intent: Feed the provisional custodian fully before protecting the household's own meal.
state_basis: Bel's hearth holds tonight's bowl turn and knows Sera's support is necessary.
reviewed_consequences: Sets a full bowl and raises Sera's recovery basis while reducing home security and increasing Nim's hidden load.

branches.actor_intent: Preserve the hearth's meal and make the custodian portion shortage inspectable.
state_basis: The bowl rotation records full, short, exchanged, refused, or returned turns.
reviewed_consequences: Sets a short bowl, improves home security, and raises record honesty.

branches.actor_intent: Use a witnessed neighbor exchange to fill the bowl without stripping one hearth.
state_basis: Low Sere hearths may exchange turns when the replacement and resulting debt are recorded.
reviewed_consequences: Fills the bowl, raises neighbor credit and record honesty, and reduces Nim's immediate load.

branches.actor_intent: Refuse food beyond the household minimum while carrying exact evidence of prior contributions.
state_basis: A returned bowl exposes a site-support failure without granting Bel technical authority.
reviewed_consequences: Returns an empty bowl, improves household security and record honesty, and raises social pressure at the site.

branches.actor_intent: Put food into Sera's hands before the ledger can treat delivery as completed care.
state_basis: Sera is visibly working and has not yet eaten; Bel controls the covered bowl.
reviewed_consequences: Raises Sera's recovery and pressure load because the sample waits while she eats.

branches.actor_intent: Make lower-step damp and missed labor part of the operational record.
state_basis: Bel witnessed the wet line and Nim's displaced Grey Bed watch.
reviewed_consequences: Raises record honesty, home security awareness, and witness coverage through an actionable household report.

branches.actor_intent: Force the ledger to name the bowl's actual state before anyone consumes or reinterprets it.
state_basis: Bel still holds the lidded bowl and the bowl-state marks are locally legible; food-first and work-for-rest choices remain gated to bowls that contain food.
reviewed_consequences: Raises record honesty and social pressure while preserving the actual full, short, or returned state.

branches.actor_intent: Perform safe instructed screen work so Sera can eat with both hands.
state_basis: Local workers may clean public outer screens; the pressure grate and technical seal remain closed.
reviewed_consequences: Raises Sera's recovery and witness coverage and lowers immediate pressure, while increasing Nim's unsupported household load.

branches.actor_intent: Complete the bounded hearth-witness interval while sending Nim to protect bedding and wait for enough hands to move the bed.
state_basis: Bel can witness from the chalk mark; Nim knows the hearth and can brace the bed.
reviewed_consequences: Raises watch coverage while reducing home security and sharply increasing Nim's hidden relief load.

branches.actor_intent: Call named lower-step neighbors into both the wall leak and the witness gap.
state_basis: Nim can carry an exact public call along the lower rail; prior exchanges can make response more credible.
reviewed_consequences: Raises neighbor credit, witness coverage, and home security while placing another carrying burden on Nim.

branches.actor_intent: End the promised short interval, protect the household, and require narrower service until relief arrives.
state_basis: The bowl carrier owes only a bounded witness interval; Sera may narrow service when support fails.
reviewed_consequences: Raises home security and record honesty, lowers watch coverage, and narrows service to reduce machine risk at a material household cost.

branches.actor_intent: Make the basin table call a better-resourced dry-step hearth before Bel leaves.
state_basis: Maro controls the household bell and basin-table work schedule; dry-step hearths share the output.
reviewed_consequences: Raises record honesty, witness coverage, home security, and delay pressure while redistributing the next interval.

branches.actor_intent: Protect Sera from another provisional-office failure by closing the turn as full.
state_basis: The ending succeeds only if food, recovery, and witness coverage make the full-turn claim true.
reviewed_consequences: Routes to supported loyalty or a hidden-cost ending based on bowl_state, sera_recovery, and watch_coverage.

branches.actor_intent: Preserve food, witness, household, and labor costs as separate facts.
state_basis: The ending succeeds only if earlier choices produced enough record honesty and witness coverage.
reviewed_consequences: Routes to an inspectable-care or incomplete-memory ending.

branches.actor_intent: Hold the household witness token until Bel's own room is safe.
state_basis: The ending succeeds only when home help arrived before pressure and delay outran the household.
reviewed_consequences: Routes to a defended household boundary or a too-late divided emergency based on home security and pressure load.

branches.actor_intent: Divide the remaining support turn into named reciprocal intervals.
state_basis: The ending succeeds only when neighbors were actually called and exchanges were kept legible.
reviewed_consequences: Routes to named reciprocal care or wishful solidarity based on neighbor credit and record honesty.

Any promotion of this fixture's evening into Kalsa historical canon
Any universalization of the forty-second bowl beyond Low Sere
Any use of the fixture as core model-training signal rather than reviewed website collateral and lore stress-test material

audit.reviewer: Codex Kalsa Hearth elaborator applying four repository reviewer prompts as separate self-review passes
review_notes: Narrative review gated food-dependent actions away from the returned-empty-bowl path, corrected the false home-security gain when Nim was sent back alone, and reconciled the named mutual-aid ending's participants.

Lore review promoted the load-bearing witness place and two distinct public signals into the Low Sere owner note, kept Nim and this evening fixture-local, and confirmed that the three-shutter dungeon clock does not advance.

Visual review added exact Ink anchors for the Warm Steps transition and Nim's arrival, added the missing witness-fold BFL prompt, and verified complete standalone character and environment descriptions.

Spatial review separated the broad bronze water-cut bell from the smaller fired-clay hearth-recall bell and aligned the scored witness place across lore, Ink, visual prompts, and the embedded two-set map.

Ink was intentionally not compiled because the pass contract forbids installing an Ink compiler; structural checks found sixteen branch labels mirrored by sixteen sidecar branches, reachable knot targets, and later reads for every declared variable.

findings.problem: The returned-empty-bowl path could select actions whose prose required Sera to eat.
findings.fix: Gated feed-first and work-for-rest choices to bowl_state >= 1.

findings.problem: Sending Nim home alone contradicted Nim's stated inability to move the bed and incorrectly increased household safety.
findings.fix: Changed the task to protecting bedding while waiting for help, reduced home_security, and preserved the increase to eldest_load.

findings.problem: The successful mutual-aid ending named four neighbor tasks while its visual group and prior call established three neighbors plus Bel.
findings.fix: Assigned three named neighbor tasks and made Bel hold the fourth quarter-turn.

findings.problem: The fixture depended on a bounded witness position and replacement signal that the authored owner-note elaboration had not yet named.
findings.fix: Added the scored witness place, broad bronze water-cut bell, and smaller fired-clay turn bell to Kalsa/Spoilers/Places/Low Sere.md.

findings.problem: A pressure knock could be mistaken for an advancement of the Ashen Intake's three-shutter clock.
findings.fix: Kept the black door closed, stated that no mark closes, preserved exactly three pale marks in every prompt, and treated the response as bounded surface isolation.

findings.problem: Nim Orra and this specific evening lack owner-note canon status.
findings.fix: Marked Nim and the evening as fixture-local in the grounding digest and mutation policy.

findings.problem: The uphill transition and Nim's arrival initially used descriptive pseudo-anchors instead of exact Ink knots.
findings.fix: Added warm_steps_route and nim_arrival knots and bound their visual_scene_id entries directly.

findings.problem: The BFL simple manifest lacked the witness-fold frame present in the visual plan.
findings.fix: Added 11_witness_fold and aligned the batch to all sixteen visual scenes.

findings.problem: Multi-angle replay requires geometry authority beyond image-model memory.
findings.fix: Embedded two fixed room models, explicit routes, ten camera slots, sightline lanes, staging slots, and branch-persistent object anchors in the visual plan.

findings.problem: One ambiguously named bell appeared to own both public water-cut warning and household replacement calls.
findings.fix: Separated a broad bronze water-cut bell at the drain station from a small fired-clay turn bell at the ration board in lore, Ink, prompts, and scene_set.

findings.problem: The visual plan called the witness position chalk while the owner note established a durable scored place.
findings.fix: Aligned all visual prompts, modifiers, routes, and sightlines to the scored witness place outside the grate.

findings.problem: The story moves between home and Cistern House while Bel cannot observe both simultaneously.
findings.fix: The scene_set routes the uphill stair through the downslope doorway and explicitly occludes the household beyond the first Warm Steps turn.
